newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE grains up as buyers ignore sterling.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE grains up as buyers ignore sterling.

text.p: LIFFE grains ended higher but off highs, after a flurry of mixed interest pushed prices up, and got the market out of the grip of currency, traders said.
Shipper buying in the afternoon, was followed by consumer and merchant interest and created a bandwagon which pushed wheat prices up, one trader said.
Most positions eased just back from highs in the final stages of trade.
"It wasn't following currency," the trader said.
On wheat, active November last traded 1.40 stg up at 87.50 stg, on volume of 214 lots, of the total 390.
September was most active on barley, with 35 of the total 75 lots. It last traded 0.45 stg higher at 78.25 stg.
A lack of farmer selling limited activity, physical market brokers said. One reckoned the market could soon start to get squeezed by a shortage of grain.
